Let \(d=x+y\). Since \(\gcd(x,y)=1\), we have \(\gcd(d,y)=1\). Modulo \(d\),
\[
(x-y)^{2016}+y^{2016}\equiv (-2y)^{2016}+y^{2016}
= y^{2016}(2^{2016}+1).
\]
Thus the divisibility condition is
\[
d \mid 2015^{2015} y^{2016}(2^{2016}+1).
\]
Since \(\gcd(d,y)=1\), this is equivalent to
\[
d \mid 2015^{2015}(2^{2016}+1).
\]
We minimize \(d=x+y\). For any divisor \(d>1\), we can take \(x=1,\ y=d-1\), so we need the smallest divisor \(>1\) of
\[
2015^{2015}(2^{2016}+1).
\]
This number is odd and not divisible by \(3\), but it is divisible by \(5\), since \(5\mid 2015\). Therefore the smallest possible \(d=x+y\) is \(5\).

Hence
\[
a+b=2015(x+y)=2015\cdot 5=10075.
\]

\[
\boxed{10075}
\]
